lessons.title: Talking About Our Favourite Toys
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a favourite toy using adjectives.
success_criteria: I can name my favourite toy.
I can use two describing words about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult describes a toy without naming it; children guess.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model describing a toy using adjectives (soft, shiny, bouncy, colourful).
lessons.independent_task: Children describe their favourite toy to a partner using at least two adjectives, then write them down.
resources_needed: toy pictures if none brought in
key_questions: What does your toy look/feel like?
Can you think of another describing word?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use 4+ adjectives in a full descriptive sentence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note adjective use and vocabulary range — evidence for ENG.SL1/ENG.W3.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite describing words found today.
lessons.home_link: Describe a toy at home using two adjectives.

lessons.title: Counting Toys to 20
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count a set of objects accurately to 20.
success_criteria: I can count objects to 20.
I can write the matching numeral.
lessons.starter_activity: Count around the class to 20.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting toy counters into groups of 10 to support counting to 20 accurately.
lessons.independent_task: Children count sets of toy counters (up to 20) and record the numeral.
key_questions: How many toys are in this set?
How did grouping in 10s help you count?

differentiation.greater_depth: Count to 30+ and compare two sets

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting range and accuracy — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Class total toy count using grouping strategy.
lessons.home_link: Count a collection of toys at home.

lessons.title: What Toys Do We Play With Today?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe types of toys played with today.
success_criteria: I can name three toys I play with.
I can sort toys into groups (e.g. electronic, non-electronic).
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss favourite toys played with at home.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the idea of sorting toys into categories (electronic vs non-electronic, indoor vs outdoor).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort picture cards of modern toys into categories and record their sorting.
key_questions: What toys do you play with most?

differentiation.greater_depth: Sort into 3+ categories and justify choices

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline understanding of 'now' toys before comparing to the past — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap categories of modern toys discussed.
lessons.home_link: List your three favourite toys at home.

lessons.title: Drawing My Favourite Toy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and draw a toy with attention to shape and detail.
success_criteria: I can draw the main shape of my toy.
I can add detail and colour.
lessons.starter_activity: Look closely at a toy from different angles.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model observational drawing, breaking a toy down into basic shapes first.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw their favourite toy (or a provided one) from observation, adding colour.
key_questions: What shapes make up your toy?

differentiation.support: Use simple shape templates as a starting guide
differentiation.greater_depth: Add shading and fine detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe observational drawing skill — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.plenary: Display toy drawings and children introduce their toy.
lessons.home_link: Draw another toy from home.

lessons.title: Writing a Toy Advertisement
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write short persuasive sentences about a toy.
success_criteria: I can write a sentence saying why my toy is good.
I can use an exciting adjective.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an example toy advert/packaging.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a persuasive sentence about a toy using exciting adjectives.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 1-2 persuasive sentences advertising their favourite toy.
key_questions: Why is your toy the best?
What exciting word could you use?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 3+ sentences with varied sentence openers

lessons.assessment_notes: Note persuasive vocabulary and sentence construction — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share adverts and vote on the most persuasive.
lessons.home_link: Write an advert for a toy at home.

lessons.title: Addition with Toy Counters
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add two single-digit numbers using concrete objects.
success_criteria: I can add two small numbers using counters.
I can write the addition number sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting on from a number.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model adding two groups of toy counters together and writing the matching number sentence (e.g. 3+2=5).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve simple addition problems using toy counters, recording number sentences.
key_questions: Can you write the number sentence?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add numbers within 20, some without counters

lessons.assessment_notes: Record addition fluency and number sentence writing — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire addition quiz using toy counters.
lessons.home_link: Practise adding small groups of toys together.

lessons.title: Interviewing About Toys
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to ask a simple question about someone's favourite toy.
success_criteria: I can ask a question about a toy.
I can report the answer back.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap asking simple questions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model asking and answering a simple interview question about toys.
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children interview each other about favourite toys and report back to the class.
key_questions: What did you ask your partner?

differentiation.support: Adult provides the question to ask
differentiation.greater_depth: Ask a follow-up question independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note question-asking and reporting skill — evidence for HIST.1/ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of interesting toy facts gathered.
lessons.home_link: Interview a family member about their favourite toy as a child (links to next week).

lessons.title: Toy Sculpture with Clay/Playdough
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to shape a simple 3D model of a toy using malleable materials.
success_criteria: I can shape a simple 3D form.
I can add detail to my model.
lessons.starter_activity: Explore squeezing and shaping playdough/clay.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model shaping a simple toy form (e.g. a ball, a simple robot) using basic techniques (rolling, pinching).
lessons.independent_task: Children create a simple 3D toy model using playdough or clay.

differentiation.greater_depth: Add fine detail and combine multiple shapes

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe 3D shaping skill and fine motor control — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.plenary: Display 3D toy models together.
lessons.home_link: Make a model with playdough or plasticine at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Toy-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read toy-themed words containing Phase 5 graphemes.
success_criteria: I can blend sounds to read toy words.
I can read a short sentence about toys.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key graphemes from the phonics baseline.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a Phase 5 grapheme, blending toy-themed words containing it.
lessons.independent_task: Children read toy-themed word and sentence cards, recording ones they found tricky.

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC toy words with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Read sentences independently and fluently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a toy-word reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading toy words over the week.

lessons.title: Subtraction with Toy Counters
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to subtract a single-digit number from a number to 10 using concrete objects.
success_criteria: I can subtract using counters.
I can write the subtraction number sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model subtracting toy counters from a group and writing the matching number sentence (e.g. 5-2=3).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve simple subtraction problems using toy counters, recording number sentences.
key_questions: Can you write the subtraction sentence?

differentiation.greater_depth: Subtract within 20, some without counters

lessons.assessment_notes: Record subtraction fluency — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire subtraction quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise taking away small groups of toys.

lessons.title: How Do Toys Work? Simple Mechanisms
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe simply how a toy moves or works.
success_criteria: I can describe how one toy moves.
I can compare two toys' mechanisms (e.g. wind-up vs battery).
lessons.starter_activity: Explore a few toys with different mechanisms (wind-up, battery, push-along).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how different toys move (winding, batteries, pushing/pulling, springs).
lessons.independent_task: Children explore and record how 2-3 different toys work/move.

differentiation.support: Explore and describe 1-2 toys with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Compare 4+ toys' mechanisms and explain differences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of simple mechanisms — evidence for HIST.1/SCI links.
lessons.plenary: Recap different ways toys can move.
lessons.home_link: Explore how a toy at home moves/works.

lessons.title: Designing a New Toy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to design a new toy on paper with labelled features.
success_criteria: I can draw a design for a new toy.
I can label at least two features.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what makes a fun toy.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sketching a toy design and labelling key features.
lessons.independent_task: Children design their own invented toy, drawing and labelling it.
key_questions: What materials would it be made from?

differentiation.support: Adult supports labelling with word bank
differentiation.greater_depth: Write a short description of how the toy works

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe design thinking and labelling — evidence for ART.2/DT links.
lessons.plenary: Share toy designs and vote on the most inventive.
lessons.home_link: Show your toy design to your family and explain it.

lessons.title: Sequencing a Story About a Toy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence and retell a simple toy-themed story.
success_criteria: I can put story pictures in order.
I can retell the story using sequencing words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sequencing words.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a short toy-themed story (e.g. a toy comes to life), modelling sequencing.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence picture cards of the story and retell it to a partner using sequencing words.

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence 5+ cards and retell independently in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for ENG.R2/W2.
lessons.plenary: One pair retells the story to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to your family.

lessons.title: Comparing Mass: Which Toy Is Heavier?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the mass of two objects using balance scales.
success_criteria: I can say which object is heavier/lighter.
I can use balance scales to check.
lessons.starter_activity: Hold two toys and guess which is heavier.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using balance scales to compare the mass of two toys.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the mass of pairs of toys using balance scales, recording results.

differentiation.greater_depth: Order 4+ toys by mass

lessons.assessment_notes: Record mass comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of heaviest/lightest toys measured.
lessons.home_link: Compare the weight of two toys at home by holding them.

lessons.title: Sorting Toys by Age Group
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort toys by the age group they are designed for.
success_criteria: I can sort a toy as for babies, young children, or older children.
I can explain my reasoning.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss toys suitable for babies vs older children.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how toys are designed differently for different ages (safety, complexity).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort toy picture cards by age group, explaining their reasoning.
resources_needed: Toy picture cards spanning age ranges
key_questions: Why is this toy for babies?
What makes a toy suitable for older children?

differentiation.support: Sort into 2 age groups with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Sort into 3+ groups and justify each choice

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reasoning and categorisation skill — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap age-appropriate toy examples.
lessons.home_link: Talk about which of your toys were for when you were younger.

lessons.title: Printing Toy Shapes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a repeated print pattern using toy-shaped stamps.
success_criteria: I can print a toy shape clearly.
I can repeat my print to make a pattern.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap pattern-making from Week 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model printing with toy-shaped sponges/stamps to create a repeating pattern.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a printed pattern using toy-shaped stamps and paint.

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a deliberate ABAB or ABC repeating pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe printing technique and pattern understanding — evidence for ART.1/MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Display printed patterns together.
lessons.home_link: Create a print pattern using any safe household stamps.

lessons.title: Toy Show and Tell Presentations
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present information about a toy clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can present information about a toy.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's toy learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation (loud voice, eye contact, key facts).
lessons.independent_task: Children present their toy design or favourite toy to a small group, answering a question.
resources_needed: Toy designs from earlier in the week
key_questions: What is special about your toy?
What question can you answer about it?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language progress since Week 1 — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all the toy presentations.
lessons.home_link: Present your toy to your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Addition, Subtraction
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, addition, and subtraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can count to 20.
I can add and subtract using counters.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of counting to 20, addition, and subtraction.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: counting toys, addition problems, subtraction problems.

differentiation.greater_depth: Independent completion with recording and extension problems

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 2 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting, adding and subtracting over the weekend.

lessons.title: Toys Now: Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about toys today learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name types of toys we play with today.
I can describe how some toys work.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's history learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about modern toys.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Toys Now' display combining toy drawings, designs, and sorting work from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about toys today?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain multiple ideas with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for HIST.1, preparing for next week's comparison to toys in the past.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'Toys Now' display.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member what toys they had that you don't have today (links to next week).

lessons.title: Art Celebration: Toy-Themed Gallery
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to reflect on and present their toy-themed artwork from the week.
success_criteria: I can talk about my favourite piece of art from this week.
I can explain the technique I used.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all art techniques used this week (drawing, sculpture, design, printing).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss reflecting on and presenting artwork.
lessons.independent_task: Children set up and present a mini gallery of their toy-themed art from the week to a partner.
key_questions: Which piece are you most proud of?

differentiation.support: Point to work and name the technique
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the process and reasoning behind choices

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective language and technique recall — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class gallery walk of toy-themed art.
lessons.home_link: Show your favourite piece of art from this week to your family.
